notes.meaning: Jesus begins a story about ten young bridesmaids waiting for a wedding feast. The bridegroom represents Jesus himself, and the wedding shows his return at the end of the age. Everyone waiting claims to look forward to his coming.

differ.view: The virgins represent the nation of Israel waiting for the Messiah at the end of the tribulation, rather than the Christian church.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The ten virgins stand for all of human society, while the bride is the Church waiting for Christ.

notes.meaning: Five bridesmaids were thoughtful and prepared, while the other five were careless. Jesus does not divide them into good and bad people, but into those who planned ahead and those who did not. True wisdom means getting ready to meet the Lord before it is too late.

The foolish bridesmaids carried their lamps or torches, but brought nothing extra to keep them burning. On the outside they looked just like the others. Their mistake was failing to make sure they had what was needed for a long wait.

differ.view: Reformed Christians understand that the foolish virgins never had true saving grace or spiritual life at all.
Methodists see the lamp as faith, which quickly dies out unless it is fueled by love.

notes.meaning: The wise bridesmaids brought jars of oil along with their torches. They knew the bridegroom might take a long time, so they prepared for any delay. Real faith looks ahead and makes sure the heart is supplied with God's life.

differ.view: The oil represents God's saving grace, which is freely given to the elect and cannot be earned.
The oil represents genuine love in the heart that keeps faith alive and growing.
The oil represents the Holy Spirit living inside true believers.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The oil represents divine grace and love joined with a life of good deeds.

notes.meaning: The bridegroom took much longer to arrive than anyone expected. Because of the long wait, all ten bridesmaids grew tired and fell asleep. The story does not blame them for sleeping, because even sincere believers grow weary during a long delay.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Some early church writers and Catholic commentaries view this sleep as physical death before the final judgment.

notes.meaning: In the middle of the night, a sudden shout woke everyone up to announce the groom's arrival. Midnight was the hour when people least expected anyone to come. In the same way, the return of Jesus will take the world by surprise.
All ten bridesmaids woke up and hurried to clean the burnt wicks of their torches. At first, both groups seemed ready to join the procession. A sudden crisis quickly reveals who is truly prepared.

The foolish bridesmaids realized their torches were flickering and going out. They begged the wise ones to share some of their oil. They discovered their terrible lack only when the moment to meet the groom had arrived.

differ.view: The dying lamps show that a person can once have genuine faith and later lose it through neglect.
The foolish virgins never had true saving grace at all, but only an outward show that eventually failed.

notes.meaning: The wise bridesmaids replied that they could not share, or no one would have enough. They told the foolish ones to go and buy oil for themselves. No one can borrow a personal relationship with God or rely on someone else's faith on judgment day.

differ.view: This answer refutes the idea that holy Christians have extra good works that can be credited to other people.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Going to those who sell oil refers to gaining the spiritual benefit of good works by showing mercy to the poor.

notes.meaning: While the foolish bridesmaids were away trying to find oil, the bridegroom arrived. Those who were ready walked inside with him to the wedding banquet, and the door was shut. When the final day comes, the time to prepare is over.

Later, the other bridesmaids returned and begged the master to open the door. Their frantic cry showed how desperate they were once they realized what they had lost. Earnest pleading comes too late once the door of heaven is closed.

The bridegroom answered firmly from inside that he did not know them. He did not recognize them as part of his wedding party because they had not walked with him. Mere outward church membership cannot take the place of being truly known and loved by Christ.

Jesus gives the main lesson of the entire story: stay alert and be ready. No human being knows the day or the hour when the Son of Man will return. True readiness means walking with God every day rather than putting off spiritual matters.

Jesus starts another story about a master who left home on a long trip. Before leaving, he called his servants together and put them in charge of his property. The master represents Jesus, who went to heaven and left his followers to manage his work on earth.

The master gave five talents of money to one servant, two to another, and one to a third, based on their ability. A single talent was a huge amount of silver, worth many years of normal wages. God gives his people different gifts and opportunities, and he expects each person to use what they receive.

differ.view: The talents do not mean saving grace itself, but outward gifts and duties, especially opportunities for Christian ministry.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic teaching stresses that God expects people to actively cooperate with his gifts and grace through their free will.

notes.meaning: The servant who received five talents immediately went to work, traded with them, and doubled his money. In the same way, the servant with two talents worked hard and gained two more. Both men showed eager obedience by using their master's wealth for his gain without delay.

The servant who received one talent went away, dug a hole in the dirt, and buried his master's silver. He did not spend the money or steal it, but he refused to do anything useful with it. People often neglect God's gifts because they think their small role does not matter.

After a long time, the master finally returned and called each servant to settle accounts. The mention of a long delay shows that Christ would not return immediately. A day of judgment is coming when every servant must explain how they used what was given to them.

The servant with five talents stepped forward gladly and handed over five more. He gave his report with joy and confidence because he had worked faithfully for his master. Believers who serve Christ with whole hearts can look forward to his return without fear.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: This servant's reward shows that human free will, aided by divine grace, truly gains merit before God.

notes.meaning: The master praised him warmly as a good and faithful servant. Because the man was faithful with a few things, the master placed him over many things and welcomed him into his own joy. The reward for faithful service to Christ is greater responsibility and eternal delight in his presence.

The servant who had received two talents came forward and reported that he had also doubled his money. His master gave him the exact same praise and the exact same reward as the first servant. God does not measure us by how much we produce compared to others, but by how faithful we are with what he gave us.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic writers note that this equal reward shows God judges each person by what was given, allowing humble believers to reach heaven just as easily as the most gifted.
